hook_text: In 2012 a group of librarians pulled off one of the greatest rescues in history. Their weapons? Metal trunks and donkey carts.
clip_script: Timbuktu, 2012. Armed groups take over the city. They smash ancient tombs. Hundreds of thousands of handwritten books, some over five hundred years old, are in danger. So librarians and families make a secret plan. Night after night they pack the manuscripts into metal trunks. Donkey carts, river boats, cars. Past checkpoints, eight hundred kilometres to the capital, Bamako. In January 2013 the attackers set fire to a library, and thousands of manuscripts burn. But most had already gone. And here is a South African twist: that library building had been built with South Africa's help, after President Thabo Mbeki visited in 2001, and Malian experts trained in Pretoria to look after the books. African history, saved by Africans.
visual_style: A whiteboard night scene: trunks loaded onto a donkey cart, a boat on the Niger, a dotted route to Bamako; a library with a small flame; a handshake between South African and Malian flags drawn simply.
pacing: Heist-movie pacing, a tense middle, an uplifting ending.
